chunk_findings.detail: The new helper imports `conftest`, while `tests/conftest.py:9` imports the helper, creating an import cycle. The helper is not importable on its own: from the `tests` directory, `python -c "import _upgrade_apply_support"` starts the helper, reaches `from conftest import run_cli`, which starts `conftest`, which reaches `from _upgrade_apply_support import old` before `old` has been defined, raising `ImportError: cannot import name 'old' from partially initialized module`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/_upgrade_apply_support.py:12

chunk_findings.detail: The conftest imports `_upgrade_apply_support` before the following line inserts the project root into `sys.path`, but the helper imports `ddflow.surfaces.cli` and other `ddflow` modules at module load time. In a source checkout where `ddflow` is not already importable from site-packages, pytest collection fails while importing conftest with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ddflow'`; the conftest’s own `sys.path.insert` is never reached.
chunk_findings.title: tests/conftest.py:9

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes the old module and adds no shim/re-export or documented rename map at the old path. This violates [r-small-files]’s requirement that a split keep the old import path and the stated requirement that golden/pin files naming the file remain valid. For example, `pytest --collect-only tests/test_upgrade_apply.py` now fails because the file is gone, and any golden snapshot or import referencing `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py` / `tests.test_upgrade_apply` fails or mismatches because collected node IDs now use the new file names.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_upgrade_apply.py (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: The split removes the original test module instead of preserving the old import path or providing a rename map, so the collected pytest ids change. For example, the old id `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py::test_applying_hooks_installs_them_backs_up_and_records` becomes `tests/test_upgrade_apply_core.py::test_applying_hooks_installs_them_backs_up_and_records` according to the manifest. Any golden/pin, selection mechanism, or external reference keyed to the old module path (the deleted file also carried the `GOVERNS` marker used by `ddflow tests --item`) will no longer match the same collected id/path, and no rename map is present in the change. This violates the stated conformance requirement [r-reuse-core] that the split keep the old import path / preserve the before-and-after test-id set.

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py` and moves these tests into `tests/test_upgrade_apply_core.py` (plus other new modules), so standard pytest node IDs change from `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py::test_x` to `tests/test_upgrade_apply_core.py::test_x`. The manifest for the whole change lists no compatibility module, golden/pin update, or documented rename map, and this file provides none. That violates the stated split requirement that collected test IDs remain the same set or be documented by a rename map, and it will break any golden/pin or CI comparison that names the old test file [r-small-files].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_upgrade_apply_core.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: The test treats “replace `Claim before you edit`” as creating a hand edit, but it never asserts that the replacement actually changed the driver file or that the first `go` call applied anything. If the driver-doc fixture/template is changed so that the magic string is absent, `driver.write_text(driver.read_text().replace(...))` writes the same bytes, the first `go` is a no-op, the snapshot contains no applied state, and the second `go` also returns `noop=True` with an unchanged tree. The test therefore passes vacuously even though it never exercised “apply a hand edit, then apply again.”

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py` and moves its wire tests into `tests/test_upgrade_apply_wire.py`, so the collected pytest node IDs change from `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py::test_...` to `tests/test_upgrade_apply_wire.py::test_...`. The stated intent requires either the same collected ID set (preserving the old import path) or a documented rename map; the 8-file manifest contains no old-path shim or rename map. Therefore any golden/pin/baseline, or CI/test-selection mechanism that names the old file or test ID, will fail to find the test after this change.

chunk_findings.detail: `tests/conftest.py` imports `_upgrade_apply_support` before the existing `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))`. `_upgrade_apply_support` immediately does `import ddflow.surfaces.cli` and other `ddflow.*` imports. When running the tests via the installed `pytest` console entry point from the repository root, the repository root is not yet on `sys.path` at that moment (pytest only ensures the `tests/` directory is importable for `conftest.py`). The result is `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ddflow'` during collection, before any test can run. This can be reproduced with `pytest tests/test_upgrade_apply_core.py` in an environment where `ddflow` is not separately installed/importable from site-packages.

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_upgrade_apply_wire.py` imports `cli` and `tree` from `_upgrade_apply_support`, but `_upgrade_apply_support` is missing from the provided diff text (it's in the manifest as a new file, but its contents are not shown in this part 6). However, the prompt says: "The other files are in the other parts: a fact that is not in this part may be in the manifest's other files, so check it there before reporting something as absent."

Let's check `tests/test_upgrade_output_commit.py`:
Line 16: `from _upgrade_apply_support import go`
The old code imported `old` as well: `from test_upgrade_apply import go, old  # noqa: F401 -- the old-version project fixture`.
The new import is: `from _upgrade_apply_support import go`.
However, the test functions in `tests/test_upgrade_output_commit.py` still take `old: Path` as a parameter (e.g., `def test_the_output_of_an_upgrade_commits_without_a_lease(old: Path) -> None:`). Since `old` fixture is no longer imported from the test module or defined in `tests/test_upgrade_output_commit.py`, pytest will raise a `FixtureLookupError: old` when running any of these tests, because `old` fixture was defined in `test_upgrade_apply.py` (which was deleted) and moving it to `_upgrade_apply_support.py` does not automatically make it available as a test fixture in other test modules unless explicitly imported or registered via conftest (pytest only loads fixtures from `conftest.py` or imported plugins/modules via `pytest_plugins`).

chunk_findings.detail: `tree()` filters volatile paths by searching `str(p)` for forward-slash substrings. On Windows, `str(Path(...))` uses backslashes, so a file such as `C:\...\old\.git\objects\xyz` does not contain `".git/"`, and a file under `...\.ddflow\local\...` does not contain `"/.ddflow/local"`. Those files are then included in the returned tree. A test that compares `tree(repo)` before/after or asserts an exact key set (for example a no-op/identical-tree test) will see extra or changing `.git` and `.ddflow/local` entries on Windows and fail. The filter should operate on `p.parts` or `p.relative_to(repo).parts`, not on OS-specific string substrings.

chunk_findings.detail: The test writes the driver with `driver.read_text().replace("Claim before you edit", "Claim when you like")` but never asserts that the replacement actually changed the file, unlike the preceding test. If the driver-doc template no longer contains the marker phrase (or `_adopted_old` leaves some unrelated drift), the first `go(old, "instructions")` may simply be a no-op or refresh unrelated drift, the second `go` will still report `noop is True`, and `tree(old) == snapshot` will hold. The test then passes without ever exercising a hand-edited driver doc, which weakens the stated split invariant that no test is weakened.

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion is `assert final["project_version"] == final["running"] and final["up_to_date"] or not final["categories"]["config"]`, which Python parses as `(project_version == running and up_to_date) or not categories.config`. If a regression leaves the config category empty but does not advance the upgrade stamp (`project_version != running`), the assertion still passes because `not final["categories"]["config"]` is true. That contradicts the test name and weakens the check that confirming the last refusal advances the stamp.

chunk_findings.detail:
`test_upgrade_apply_wire.py` imports `cli` and `tree` from `_upgrade_apply_support`, but `_upgrade_apply_support` is missing from the provided diff text (it's in the manifest as a new file, but its contents are not shown in this part 6). However, the prompt says: "The other files are in the other parts: a fact that is not in this part may be in the manifest's other files, so check it there before reporting something as absent."

Let's check `tests/test_upgrade_output_commit.py`:
Line 16: `from _upgrade_apply_support import go`
The old code imported `old` as well: `from test_upgrade_apply import go, old  # noqa: F401 -- the old-version project fixture`.
The new import is: `from _upgrade_apply_support import go`.
However, the test functions in `tests/test_upgrade_output_commit.py` still take `old: Path` as a parameter (e.g., `def test_the_output_of_an_upgrade_commits_without_a_lease(old: Path) -> None:`). Since `old` fixture is no longer imported from the test module or defined in `tests/test_upgrade_output_commit.py`, pytest will raise a `FixtureLookupError: old` when running any of these tests, because `old` fixture was defined in `test_upgrade_apply.py` (which was deleted) and moving it to `_upgrade_apply_support.py` does not automatically make it available as a test fixture in other test modules unless explicitly imported or registered via conftest (pytest only loads fixtures from `conftest.py` or imported plugins/modules via `pytest_plugins`).

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes the old test module and replaces it with new files, but the visible change adds no compatibility shim at `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py` and no ID-preserving hook in `tests/conftest.py` (the conftest diff only adds the `old` fixture). Pytest node IDs include the file path, so an old ID such as `tests/test_upgrade_apply.py::test_the_knob_defaults_are_the_decided_ones` becomes `tests/test_upgrade_apply_knobs.py::test_the_knob_defaults_are_the_decided_ones`. A golden/pin that pins collected IDs or any invocation like `pytest tests/test_upgrade_apply.py` therefore fails. This violates the stated conformance requirement that the split keep the old import path or provide a documented rename map [r-small-files].

chunk_findings.detail: `tree()` filters volatile paths by searching `str(p)` for forward-slash substrings. On Windows, `str(Path(...))` uses backslashes, so a file such as `C:\...\old\.git\objects\xyz` does not contain `".git/"`, and a file under `...\.ddflow\local\...` does not contain `"/.ddflow/local"`. Those files are then included in the returned tree. A test that compares `tree(repo)` before/after or asserts an exact key set (for example a no-op/identical-tree test) will see extra or changing `.git` and `.ddflow/local` entries on Windows and fail. The filter should operate on `p.parts` or `p.relative_to(repo).parts`, not on OS-specific string substrings.

chunk_findings.detail: The test writes the driver with `driver.read_text().replace("Claim before you edit", "Claim when you like")` but never asserts that the replacement actually changed the file, unlike the preceding test. If the driver-doc template no longer contains the marker phrase (or `_adopted_old` leaves some unrelated drift), the first `go(old, "instructions")` may simply be a no-op or refresh unrelated drift, the second `go` will still report `noop is True`, and `tree(old) == snapshot` will hold. The test then passes without ever exercising a hand-edited driver doc, which weakens the stated split invariant that no test is weakened.

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion is `assert final["project_version"] == final["running"] and final["up_to_date"] or not final["categories"]["config"]`, which Python parses as `(project_version == running and up_to_date) or not categories.config`. If a regression leaves the config category empty but does not advance the upgrade stamp (`project_version != running`), the assertion still passes because `not final["categories"]["config"]` is true. That contradicts the test name and weakens the check that confirming the last refusal advances the stamp.

chunk_findings.detail: The test accepts `out["exit"] in (0, 2, 3)` but then requires `set(ids(out, "applied"))` to equal all pending `UP.AGENT` repair ids and requires no `UP.AGENT` repair to remain in the plan. Exit code 2 is the unavailable-repair case (as exercised by `test_a_repair_that_could_not_run_exits_2_not_0` in this same file); when a pending agent repair is unavailable, that repair is not applied and remains pending, so those assertions fail.
